electric.current.description: Current through an element, conventional direction.

electric.resistance.description: Resistance of an element or of a reduced combination.

electric.emf.description: Electromotive force of a source, before any internal drop.

electric.power.description: Power dissipated or delivered by an element.

electric.capacitance.description: Capacitance of a capacitor or reduced combination.

electric.time_constant.description: RC time constant of a resistor-capacitor pair.

electric.energy_stored.description: Energy stored in a capacitor's field.

em.electric_field.description: Electric field vector at a point.

em.electric_field_magnitude.description: Magnitude of the electric field at a point.

em.potential_difference.description: Potential difference across a pair of points or plates.

em.magnetic_field.description: Magnetic flux density vector at a point.

em.magnetic_field_magnitude.description: Magnitude of the magnetic flux density.

em.electric_flux.description: Electric flux through a closed surface.

em.cyclotron_radius.description: Radius of the circular path of a charge in a uniform magnetic field.

em.cyclotron_period.description: Period of revolution of a charge in a uniform magnetic field.

env.gravity.description: Gravitational field of the surroundings, +Y up. Zero for the idealised case.

env.wind_velocity.description: Bulk velocity of the surrounding medium.

env.relative_permittivity.description: Permittivity of the medium relative to vacuum. 1 is vacuum, air is ~1.0006, water ~80. Dividing Coulomb's law by this is why immersing the same charges in water weakens the field.

env.air_density.description: Density of the surrounding medium. Zero means no drag.

geometry.position.description: Position of an object in the scene frame.

geometry.offset.description: Displacement of one object's centre from another's.

geometry.radius.description: Radius of a sphere, shell, cavity or circular path.

geometry.separation_plates.description: Gap between the plates of a parallel-plate arrangement.

geometry.direction.description: Unit vector giving the direction of a uniform field or axis. +Y is up, matching the renderer, so the default points from a top plate down to a bottom one.

geometry.cross_section.description: Area presented to the oncoming medium. Zero by default, which is what makes drag opt-in: a problem that does not mention air gets exactly no drag force.

kinematics.distance.description: Path length or magnitude of displacement.

kinematics.velocity.description: Rate of change of position, with direction.

kinematics.acceleration.description: Rate of change of velocity, with direction.

mechanics.force.description: Net force acting on an object.

mechanics.force_em.description: Electromagnetic contribution to the net force on a body.

mechanics.force_gravity.description: Gravitational contribution (weight) to the net force on a body.

mechanics.force_drag.description: Drag contribution from motion relative to the surrounding medium.

mechanics.drag_coefficient.description: Shape-dependent drag coefficient. About 0.47 for a sphere.

energy.potential_electric.description: Electric potential energy of a charge.

k_e.cite: SI 2019 exact (derived from exact c and mu_0 definition)

g_vec.description: Standard gravitational acceleration as a vector. +Y is up, matching the WebXR and three.js convention the renderer uses, so a kernel-computed vector needs no axis swap downstream.

pi_const.description: Circle constant, as a dimensionless binding.

battery.label: Battery
battery.description: An ideal source of constant emf. Two terminals; current leaves the positive one. Ideal here means zero internal resistance, which the assumption list on every formula states plainly.

resistor.label: Resistor
resistor.description: An ohmic element: the voltage across it is proportional to the current through it. The workhorse of the chapter and the first thing a student picks up off the shelf.

lamp.label: Lamp
lamp.description: A resistive element that visibly brightens with dissipated power. Physically a resistor; pedagogically much better, because the answer is something you can see rather than read.

capacitor.label: Capacitor
capacitor.description: An element storing charge in proportion to the voltage across it.

series_pair.label: Series combination
series_pair.description: Two elements wired end to end, so the same current passes through both and their voltages add. Created by the student's own wiring; carries a resistance of its own, so it can be a member of a further combination.

em.potential_difference.note: a problem may state the supply voltage across a combination

parallel_pair.label: Parallel combination
parallel_pair.description: Two elements across the same two nodes, so they share a voltage and their currents add. Carries a resistance of its own for the same compositional reason as a series pair.

em.potential_difference.note: a problem may state the supply voltage across a combination

circuit_loop.label: Circuit loop
circuit_loop.description: A closed loop: one source driving one resistive thing, which may itself be a whole reduced network. This is the component the wiring interaction produces when the student closes the circuit, and it is where the current the whole chapter is about actually lives.

em.potential_difference.note: a problem may state the supply voltage directly

ammeter.label: Ammeter
ammeter.description: Reads the current through the element it is placed in series with. Ideal: zero resistance, so inserting it does not change the circuit. A tool is an ordinary component, so this reading resolves through exactly the same machinery as a derived current.

voltmeter_dc.label: Voltmeter
voltmeter_dc.description: Reads the potential difference across the element it is placed in parallel with. Ideal: infinite resistance, so it draws no current.

point_charge.label: Point charge
point_charge.description: An idealised charge with no extent. The canonical field source; everything else in electrostatics is a superposition of these.

charged_particle.label: Charged particle
charged_particle.description: A charge with mass, free to move. Both a field source and the thing that responds to a field — which is precisely why the field -> force -> trajectory chain needs no special case.

kinematics.distance.note: a problem may state the distance travelled

kinematics.time.note: a problem may state the elapsed time

electron.label: Electron
electron.description: An electron, with charge and mass fixed by nature rather than by the problem.

kinematics.distance.note: a problem may state the distance travelled

kinematics.time.note: a problem may state the elapsed time

parallel_plate_capacitor.label: Parallel-plate capacitor
parallel_plate_capacitor.description: Two oppositely charged plates. Away from the edges the field between them is uniform, which makes this the standard way to produce a known constant field in a problem.

uniform_field_region.label: Uniform field region
uniform_field_region.description: A region of stated uniform field, for problems that give the field directly.

uniform_magnetic_field_region.label: Uniform magnetic field region
uniform_magnetic_field_region.description: A region of stated uniform magnetic flux density.

uniform_charged_sphere.label: Uniformly charged insulating sphere
uniform_charged_sphere.description: A sphere of uniform volume charge density. Non-conducting, so the charge stays put and the interior field is non-zero and linear in r.

spherical_cavity_in_charged_sphere.label: Spherical cavity in a uniformly charged sphere
spherical_cavity_in_charged_sphere.description: A spherical hole carved out of a uniformly charged insulating sphere. By superposition the field everywhere inside the cavity is uniform, equal to rho*a/(3*eps0) along the offset vector a from the sphere's centre to the cavity's. This is the flagship case: no simulation library contains it, and a charge released inside undergoes exact constant-acceleration projectile motion.

conducting_shell.label: Conducting spherical shell
conducting_shell.description: A charged conductor with a hollow interior. The field inside the cavity is exactly zero — electrostatic shielding — whatever the shell's charge or the external field.

infinite_charged_plane.label: Infinite charged plane
infinite_charged_plane.description: An infinite sheet of uniform surface charge density. Its field is uniform and independent of distance, which is why it is the standard idealisation for a large plate.

infinite_charged_line.label: Infinite charged line
infinite_charged_line.description: An infinite straight line of uniform linear charge density.

environment.label: Environment
environment.description: The surrounding medium and fields. Defaults are an idealised vacuum with no gravity, which is what textbook electrostatics problems assume -- stated here as an editable value instead of a footnote.

field_probe.label: Field probe
field_probe.description: A massless, chargeless point placed in the world to read the field there. The canonical "where" for a field question; carries no charge of its own so it never perturbs the scene.

voltmeter.label: Voltmeter
voltmeter.description: Reads the potential difference between two points. Ideal — draws no charge.

ruler.label: Ruler
ruler.description: Reads a distance or displacement in the scene.

parallel.R_from_members.note: The product-over-sum form rather than the reciprocal sum, because it is one expression instead of two and the dimension checker can verify it directly.

series.C_from_members.note: Capacitors combine the opposite way round to resistors — in series they reduce.

loop.R_from_load.note: The loop's total resistance is its load's, whatever that load reduced from. Trivial as algebra, essential as a link: it is what carries a reduced network's resistance into the loop where the current lives.

loop.I_from_V_R.note: The whole chapter in one line — once the network has reduced, the current falls out.

series.I_shared_to_member.note: In series the current is common, so a member inherits the group's current. Together with the member_b variant this is how a reading on one element reaches the other.

loop.I_shared_to_load.note: A single loop's current passes through its load, which is how the answer reaches a part.

power.P_from_V_R.note: Three forms of the same law. They are NOT alternative paths in the multi-path sense — all three cite joule_heating, so the resolver's law-set dedup collapses them to one. That is correct: picking V^2/R over I^2*R is an algebraic convenience, not different physics.

coulomb.E_mag_from_point_charge.note: The inverse square is the whole claim. A 1/r**3 slip here is dimensionally detectable, which is why the compiler compares this expression's inferred dimension against the declared solves_for property before the formula is ever used.

plates.E_mag_at_charge.note: In a uniform region the field at an enclosed object is the region's field. Trivial as algebra, essential as a link: it is what carries a field value across the `inside` relation.

sphere.E_mag_outside.note: Outside a spherically symmetric charge, the field is that of a point charge at its centre.

cavity.E_vec_uniform.note: The cavity field. Treat the holed sphere as a full sphere of density rho plus a sphere of density -rho filling the cavity. Inside a uniform sphere E = rho*r/(3*eps0) measured from its own centre, so the two contributions leave exactly rho*a/(3*eps0) along the offset a -- independent of position. Uniform field inside the hole, hence exact projectile motion for a charge released there. This is the case the market has no simulation for.

shield.E_mag_inside_conductor_cavity.note: Exactly zero, whatever the shell carries and whatever surrounds it. The formula needs no inputs at all: its entire precondition is the `inside_cavity_of` relation to a conductor, which scope/via/role_kinds already state. A literal zero is dimensionally polymorphic -- the zero element belongs to every dimension space -- so the dimension checker admits it against a V/m target without weakening anything else.

field.E_vec_from_magnitude_and_direction.note: A magnitude plus a direction is a vector. Trivial, but it is what reconnects the scalar plate-field chain to the vector force chain, and the renderer samples the result to draw field arrows.

lorentz.F_vec_electric.note: The link that makes the whole project cross-domain. `q` is electromagnetic, the result is mechanical, and the formula knows about neither domain -- only about property keys.

gravity.F_vec_from_env.note: Binds the scene's environment rather than a constant, so the weight a body feels is whatever the user has set gravity to. With the default [0,0,0] this is exactly zero, which is the idealisation textbook electrostatics problems assume.

drag.F_vec_from_env.exprText: -0.5 * rho * Cd * A * mag(v - v_wind) * (v - v_wind)
drag.F_vec_from_env.note: Wind acts only through the RELATIVE velocity v - v_wind, so a body drifting with the wind feels nothing. Both air density and cross-section default to zero, which makes drag opt-in: every existing problem gets exactly zero without having to say so.

force.net_from_contributions.note:
Superposition as an actual sum. Separating the electric and gravitational contributions is what keeps this ONE derivation instead of two rival paths that would disagree the moment gravity stopped being zero.
Drag is deliberately NOT in this sum. It only exists when the scene states a velocity, an area and a medium density, and a chain resolver cannot express "include this term only if it resolves" -- an optional contribution would either manufacture a phantom zero path or make two net formulas disagree. `mechanics.force_drag` is therefore derivable on its own and visualised on its own, and folding it in is work for the equation assembler (Engine B), where contributions are collected rather than chained. Honest limitation, recorded here rather than papered over.

kin.v_final_from_u_a_s.note: The time-free form. Where the energy route is also available this gives a second, genuinely different derivation of the same answer -- a real alternative path, not an algebraic rearrangement, because it cites kinematics where the other cites energy conservation.

kin.distance_across_plates.note: A charge released at one plate and arriving at the other has travelled the gap. Geometry rather than physics, but it has to be a cited step or the kinematics route to final speed would contain an unexplained number.

kin.displacement_from_u_a_t.note: The vector form -- this is what the renderer samples to draw a curved trajectory.

energy.work_from_q_pd.note: Work done on a charge crossing the full gap. Pairs with energy.K_from_work_at_rest and energy.v_from_K_m to give the energy route to final speed -- the alternative to the kinematics route, citing a different law.

cyclotron.period.note: Independent of speed -- the fact that makes the cyclotron work.

ohms_law.label: Ohm's law
ohms_law.statement: For an ohmic conductor the current through it is proportional to the potential difference across it, with the resistance as the constant of proportionality: V = I*R.

kirchhoff_current_law.label: Kirchhoff's current law
kirchhoff_current_law.statement: The algebraic sum of currents entering any node is zero: charge does not accumulate at a junction. This is what makes currents add in a parallel combination.

kirchhoff_voltage_law.label: Kirchhoff's voltage law
kirchhoff_voltage_law.statement: The algebraic sum of potential differences around any closed loop is zero: energy per unit charge returns to where it started. This is what makes voltages add in a series combination.

series_resistance.label: Resistances in series add
series_resistance.statement: Two elements carrying the same current present the sum of their resistances, because their potential differences add while the current is common: R = R_a + R_b.

parallel_resistance.label: Resistances in parallel combine reciprocally
parallel_resistance.statement: Two elements across the same pair of nodes present R_a*R_b/(R_a + R_b), because their currents add while the potential difference is common. The result is always smaller than either part.

joule_heating.label: Joule heating
joule_heating.statement: A resistive element dissipates electrical energy as heat at a rate P = I*V, equivalently I^2*R or V^2/R. Which of the three forms the resolver reaches for depends only on what the problem happens to give.

capacitor_definition.label: Definition of capacitance
capacitor_definition.statement: The charge stored on a capacitor is proportional to the potential difference across it, Q = C*V, and the energy held in its field is C*V^2/2.

rc_time_constant.label: RC time constant
rc_time_constant.statement: A resistor charging a capacitor does so with characteristic time tau = R*C, after which the capacitor has reached 1 - 1/e of its final charge.

coulombs_law.label: Coulomb's law
coulombs_law.statement: The electrostatic force between two point charges acts along the line joining them, with magnitude proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of their separation.

gauss_law_electric.label: Gauss's law for electricity
gauss_law_electric.statement: The electric flux through any closed surface equals the enclosed charge divided by the vacuum permittivity. Its consequences fix the field of every symmetric charge distribution.

superposition_electric.label: Superposition of electric fields
superposition_electric.statement: The field of a composite distribution is the vector sum of the fields of its parts. This is what makes the cavity construction legitimate: a sphere with a cavity is a full sphere plus a negative sphere filling the cavity.

lorentz_force.label: Lorentz force law
lorentz_force.statement: A charge q moving with velocity v through fields E and B experiences force q(E + v x B).

newton_second_law.label: Newton's second law
newton_second_law.statement: The net force on a body equals its mass times its acceleration.

kinematics_constant_acceleration.label: Kinematics under constant acceleration
kinematics_constant_acceleration.statement: While acceleration is constant, velocity is linear in time and displacement is quadratic; and v^2 = u^2 + 2*a*s eliminates time entirely.

work_energy_theorem.label: Work-energy theorem
work_energy_theorem.statement: The work done by the net force on a body equals the change in its kinetic energy.

conservation_of_energy.label: Conservation of energy
conservation_of_energy.statement: In an isolated system the total energy is constant; a charge falling through a potential difference converts electric potential energy into kinetic energy exactly.

electric_potential_definition.label: Definition of electric potential
electric_potential_definition.statement: Potential is potential energy per unit charge; the work to move a charge between two points is the charge times the potential difference.

uniform_field_between_plates.label: Uniform field between parallel plates
uniform_field_between_plates.statement: Away from the edges, the field between oppositely charged parallel plates is uniform with magnitude equal to the potential difference divided by the separation.

shielding_conductor_cavity.label: Electrostatic shielding
shielding_conductor_cavity.statement: The electrostatic field inside a cavity within a conductor, with no charge in the cavity, is exactly zero regardless of the external field or the conductor's own charge.

circular_motion_magnetic.label: Circular motion in a uniform magnetic field
circular_motion_magnetic.statement: A charge moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field travels a circle whose radius is mv/(qB) and whose period is independent of speed.

definition_magnitude.label: Magnitude of a vector quantity
definition_magnitude.statement: A scalar magnitude property is the Euclidean norm of its vector counterpart. Bookkeeping, not physics, but it must be cited like anything else so no trace step is unexplained.

newton_gravitation_uniform.label: Weight in a uniform gravitational field
newton_gravitation_uniform.statement: A body of mass m in a uniform gravitational field g experiences a force m*g directed along the field. Uniform is the right idealisation on a bench: g varies by less than a part in a million across a desk.

superposition_of_forces.label: Superposition of forces
superposition_of_forces.statement: The net force on a body is the vector sum of the forces acting on it, each computed as if the others were absent. This is why an electric force and a weight can be derived independently and then added.

medium_permittivity.label: Permittivity of the medium
medium_permittivity.statement: In a uniform dielectric the electric field of a given charge is reduced by the medium's relative permittivity. The same two charges in water attract about eighty times less strongly than in vacuum.

quadratic_drag.label: Quadratic drag through a medium
quadratic_drag.statement: A body moving at velocity v through a medium of density rho, with the medium itself moving at v_wind, feels a force -0.5*rho*C_d*A*|v - v_wind|*(v - v_wind): opposing the RELATIVE motion and growing with its square. Wind enters only through that relative velocity, which is why a body moving with the wind feels no drag at all.
